Enhanced diligence for PEPs; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation; ongoing monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online portal: https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Name must comply with Charter of the French Language; require French legal designation 'société en commandite' or abbreviation 'S.E.C.'/'L.P.'; transliteration to Latin script requires certified translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: or any term implying incorporation, crown/state endorsement, or regulated activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection by Registraire des entreprises, applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Registraire within the statutory period, then appeal to Court of Québec (Chambre administrative et de l'arbitrage) under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and Administrative Justice Act (CQLR c J-3); appeal must be written, state grounds, attach rejection notice; alternatively revise/resubmit name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only with a genuine Quebec physical registered office or registered agent; not a substitute for operational substance. For low-risk hardware business, virtual office acceptable but requires clear records and physical custody of documents in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5–10% likelihood within first 12–18 months; triggered by tax audit, customs, or consumer safety matters; no sectoral licensing requirement).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), Book 10 Title 2 on Partnerships (Articles 2161-2194) and registration formalities
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Formation of a Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; contributions determined by partners and may be placed in escrow
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby subscribes to the initial capital contribution of one thousand Canadian dollars (CAD 1,000) as the general partner's interest in the limited partnership; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the limited partnership is adopted at [Insert full Quebec address], Quebec, Canada; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Insert Name of General Partner], of [Insert Address], is appointed as the sole General Partner of the limited partnership and is authorized to appoint any necessary officers, execute all documents, and manage the business and affairs of the limited partnership in accordance with the Civil Code of Québec and the Partnership Agreement; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Partner is empowered to open bank accounts, enter into contracts, and handle all operational and compliance matters. This resolution was passed by the General Partner on [Insert Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Declaration of Formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal at registre-entreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the official Declaration of Formation of a Limited Partnership including general partner details, capital, and registered office address. Have the General Partner sign the declaration. Submit the form electronically via the REQ portal with the filing fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide missing information or resubmit the form with corrections within the allowed period

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire safety service, structural load inspections, and workplace clearance from CNESST

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; and for Quebec, Revenu Québec, through clicSÉRIE-affaires at revenuquebec.ca, with enterprise registration administered by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Quebec Limited Partnership must first obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. It must then obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account by submitting Form RC1 through the CRA's Business Registration Online portal, by mail, or by fax. For QST, the partnership must register with Revenu Québec using the LM-102 form or clicSÉRIE-affaires; registration can be completed by the general partner or an authorized Canadian agent. If annual worldwide taxable supplies are CAD 30,000 or less, registration is not mandatory for GST/HST/QST, but voluntary registration is commercially necessary to recover input tax credits and to zero-rate exports. Quebec does not impose any minimum capital requirement for limited partnerships.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box entity election. A limited partnership is fiscally transparent by statute under subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act: income is computed at the partnership level and allocated to partners. Partners may elect, through the partnership agreement, the allocation of taxable income and losses, subject to anti-avoidance and reasonableness rules. A non-resident partner may elect under section 216 of the Income Tax Act to compute Canadian income tax on an actual net basis for certain Canadian property income; for active business income, the partnership files Form T5013 and each partner reports its allocated share. For GST/HST and QST, eligible small registrants may elect the Quick Method and simplified accounting rules, but no hybrid-mismatch election is available to Canadian limited partnerships.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST), administered by Revenu Québec under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter or over the last four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold). The threshold may be bypassed for imported taxable goods or taxable real property.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing. GST/HST and QST are enforced through audit-based compliance. Invoices must contain prescribed content under ETA section 223 and QSRA section 450, including the supplier's name, BN/NEQ, invoice date, description of goods, and tax amounts. No PEPPOL or equivalent standard is mandatory. Revenu Québec may require specified electronic records on audit, but pre-clearance of invoices is not part of the Canadian indirect tax regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered supplier may zero-rate the sale of tangible personal property exported from Canada under subsection 23(1) of the Excise Tax Act, provided the goods are removed from Canada and the supplier maintains proof of export. Delivery to a common carrier for shipment outside Canada is sufficient if the carrier's bill of lading names a destination outside Canada. Offshore services rendered to non-residents and services relating to exported goods are generally zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V. QST zero-rating follows the same factual export test. The goods must not be consumed, used, or retained in Canada prior to export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs B13A Export Declaration or CBSA Authorized Exporter (AER) report where required by threshold or control type
Commercial invoice stating HS code under ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930, product description, quantity, and export sale price
Bill of Lading or air waybill showing the ultimate destination outside Canada
Packing list and customs broker records evidencing export from Quebec
Carrier-issued proof of delivery or destination-country customs entry
Foreign exchange transaction advice or bank inward remittance certificate confirming payment in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess GST/HST and QST within four years, extended to ten years for misrepresentation, wilful default, or fraud. Zero-ratings are clawed back where export documentation is incomplete, commercial terms are not supported, or goods are diverted for domestic use. Civil penalties for false statements amount to 10% of the misstated tax for carelessness and 50% for gross negligence; ETA section 280 and section 285.1 permit additional penalties of up to $20,000 plus 100% of net tax and prescribed interest. Criminal prosecution under ITA section 239 and ETA section 403 may result in fines up to $500,000 and imprisonment up to five years; Quebec imposes equivalent QST clawback, penalty, and fraud provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) ...

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration and annual registration fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a limited partnership, within 30 days after the anniversary of its registration date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment charges and default notices may apply. Failure to file required annual declarations, particularly for two consecutive years, may result in cancellation of the registration after the statutory notice period, generally including a 60-day compliance period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due five months after the partnership fiscal period-end where the filing obligation applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply, including penalties based on the number of partners and days outstanding. Repeated non-compliance may trigger assessments, information demands, and audit activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (Form TP-600-V), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due five months after the partnership fiscal period-end where the Quebec filing obligation applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest may apply. Revenu Québec may issue assessments, require additional information, and commence compliance or audit procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST and QST annual returns, where annual reporting is assigned
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the filing and payment deadline assigned to the partnership's GST/HST and QST reporting periods; annual filing is not automatic for every registrant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, arrears interest, collection measures, and possible suspension or cancellation of tax accounts may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory independent-audit requirement applies solely because a Quebec limited partnership carries on an ordinary private business. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, a lender, an investor, securities legislation, or a contractual reporting undertaking.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises under Canadian GAAP are generally applicable to private entities. IFRS applies where the partnership elects or is required to report under IFRS, including applicable publicly accountable or securities-regulated circumstances. Tax returns use prescribed Canadian federal and Quebec tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The partnership must review beneficial ownership, control, general-partner, limited-partner, and partnership-interest information before each annual updating declaration. Ultimate beneficial owner information must be reported to the Quebec Enterprise Register where required and updated after a change, generally within 30 days. A transfer of a partnership interest must be assessed for a change in ultimate beneficiary or control and reflected in the applicable register filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners and partnership interests
Register of General Partners and Limited Partners
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners and control information
Minutes or written resolutions of partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 500-1,500 per year for a Quebec business address, mail handling, and compliance support; Quebec limited partnerships generally do not require a separate statutory registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 where no audit is required; typically 5,000-20,000 if an independent audit is required by agreement, financing, investors, or applicable regulation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the limited partnership level (flow-through); combined federal/Quebec general corporate headline for a taxable corporate partner is 26.5% (federal 15% after abatement plus Quebec 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level tax because the LP is tax-transparent. A Canadian-controlled private corporation partner may claim the federal small-business rate of 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income and the Quebec reduced rate of 5%, producing a combined 14% effective rate. SR&ED investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs) and the Quebec interactive digital media tax credit (up to 30% refundable) are available for eligible robotic-AI software/content development. Losses are generally allocated to partners; the federal/Quebec non-capital loss carryforward is substantively 20 years, but the pipeline schema field is populated as 5 for risk-scoring classification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Statement of Partnership Income, T5013 Summary and T5013 Supplementary; filed electronically via CRA My Business Account / Represent a Client (Internet File Transfer) or EDI; mandatory electronic filing when more than 50 T5013 slips are issued.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end. For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the deadline is May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA business number (BN), legal entity name of the limited partnership, mailing address, and fiscal period end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the BN issued to the LP. A non-resident partnership with Canadian-source income must request a CRA non-resident account and use the appropriate 'NR' designation on all slips.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of the end of the partnership's taxation/fiscal year; must be identical for all partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly formed LP, select a fiscal period end no later than 12 months after commencement; non-resident partners report their allocated share in their own taxation year under the applicable treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Partner Information and Profit-Sharing Ratios
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, business number or social insurance number for each partner, class of interest (general vs limited), and percentage interests in income, loss, and capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, enter country of residence, treaty status, and restrict to passive limited-interest percentages unless the partner actively participates in management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from robotic-AI companion pet sales, embedded software licensing, post-sale support, and related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source revenue. Cross-border cost allocations require arm's-length support and T106 disclosure when aggregated related-party transactions equal or exceed CAD 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Net Income/Loss Allocation and At-Risk Amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss computed under ITA s.96, allocated to each partner, showing the limited partner's at-risk amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners may deduct losses only to the extent of their at-risk amount; income allocations must be economically proportionate to capital contribution and reflect assumption of risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Part XIII Payments to Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocated Canadian-source business income and any interest or royalties paid or credited to non-resident partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross amounts, treaty-reduced amounts, and supporting Form NR301/NR302 and the Certificate of Residence. Absent a treaty exemption, withhold 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late filing: CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500) for the T5013 return; CAD 25 per day per missing T5013 slip up to CAD 2,500; CAD 100 for failure to file electronically when required; interest accrues on any unremitted partner withholding; gross negligence attracts a 50% penalty on misreported amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-5013 – Quebec Partnership Information Return (Déclaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes); filed via Revenu Québec 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' (clicSÛR).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end, aligned with the federal T5013 deadline; a December 31 year-end requires filing by May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), CRA business number, establishment address, fiscal-period end, and legal form of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LP has no Quebec establishment but derives Quebec-source income, still register with Revenu Québec; enter the foreign head-office address and the non-resident partner's country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B – Allocation of Income to Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian-source income, Quebec-source income, and the allocation percentage assigned to each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same allocation as in the federal T5013. Quebec-source allocation must follow the wage/gross-revenue/capital formula used by Revenu Québec for corporate allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of Quebec tax withheld from non-resident partners, instalments paid, and refundable credits claimed by partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners attach evidence of treaty relief, including the federal NR301/NR302 confirmation and Certificate of Residence, to avoid over-withholding by the general partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authentication of the return by the general partner or authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the general partner is itself non-resident, it must appoint a Quebec/Canadian agent with a valid power of attorney for service of notices and assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec: late information return penalties of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; partner-level late filing penalties of 5% of the tax payable plus 1% per month up to 12%; false declarations may attract a 50% penalty under the Quebec Taxation Act and revocation of limited-partner status.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under ITA Part XIII on Canadian-source payments to non-resident persons; for a limited partnership, no dividend withholding arises at the LP level, but a non-resident partner's allocated share of Canadian-source business income is subject to 25% Part XIII withholding unless reduced by treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident partner must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty country's tax authority, submit CRA Form NR301 (application for reduced Part XIII withholding) or NR302 (waiver/exemption), and, for US partners, a Form W-8BEN-E or W-8IMY. The general partner must attach these documents to the T5013 and CO-5013 and apply the reduced rate at source; refunds are obtained by filing the appropriate federal and Quebec returns with treaty evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory: interest 25%, royalties 25%. Canada–US Treaty: interest generally 0% (subject to participating-debt and non-arm's-length exceptions); industrial royalties and software royalties 0%; most other treaty countries apply 10%. For an AI pet robot with embedded software, royalties for embedded software may qualify for the software/industrial royalty exemption if the beneficial owner is a treaty resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Form T106 and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation are required when the aggregate fair market value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with non-resident related parties equals or exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year. Canada does not maintain separate Local File/Master File filing thresholds; the CRA may request Local File/Master File-style information for material controlled transactions at any time and expects production within three months.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); it enforces substance through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245), treaty-shopping limitation under the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, and the 'carrying on business in Canada' test. A Quebec LP must maintain a physical office, employees, bank accounts, books and records, and board-level decision-making in Quebec; otherwise the CRA and Revenu Québec may disregard the partnership, reallocate income, or deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Suppression of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing Canadian-source revenue from AI pet robot sales, fabricating expenses, or misallocating partnership income to non-resident partners through backdated or false documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictable offence under ITA s.239(1): fine of not less than 50% and up to 200% of the tax evaded, plus imprisonment for up to five years; civil reassessment with gross-negligence penalty of 50% and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is jointly and severally liable for partnership debts and penalties; directors of a corporate general partner may be assessed under ITA s.227.1 for unremitted amounts; limited partners who participate in management lose the limited-liability shield and may face travel restrictions pending prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late / Non-Filing of Partnership Returns and Withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file T5013, CO-5013, or T106, or failing to withhold and remit 25% Part XIII tax on distributions and allocations to non-resident partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal and Quebec late-filing penalties (CAD 25/day up to CAD 2,500), T106 penalty of CAD 100 per month up to CAD 2,500, plus interest; failure-to-withhold penalties of 10% of the unwithheld amount, increasing to 20% for gross negligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding taxes, even after the LP is dissolved; officers who directed the withholding failure face personal monetary penalties and no claim to corporate-indemnification protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement / Abusive Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length prices for components, embedded software royalties, or management fees from a non-resident related party, thereby stripping Canadian taxable income from the LP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to the arm's-length price; transfer-pricing penalty under ITA s.247(3) equal to 10% of the net adjustment; denial of deduction under GAAR; retroactive interest; and penalties under Quebec law for knowingly false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners who caused or acquiesced in the mispricing may be jointly liable for the penalty; active limited partners are treated as general partners and cannot hide behind the LP's corporate shield.
